label: myadhd.my
caption:
Forgot one thing. Spent all evening calling yourself useless.

Years of being told to try harder can leave a loud voice in your head. Swipe for where it comes from, and three ways to talk back to it.

If this sounded like your brain, come sit with people who get it. Our group is in my bio 👇

Save this for the next time you are hard on yourself.

#adhd #adhdmalaysia #myadhd #adhdadult #selfcompassion

slides.title:
Why am I so
hard on
[[myself]]?
slides.sub: That voice learned its lines a long time ago.

slides.title:
You heard it
[[a lot]]
slides.body: "Try harder." "Why are you like this?" "So smart, if only you focused." Hear it enough as a kid, and it becomes your own voice.

slides.title:
One slip
becomes [[the story]]
slides.body: You forget a bill, and the voice says you forget everything. One small miss gets filed as proof of a much bigger story.

slides.title:
It thinks it
is [[helping]]
slides.body: The voice says it is keeping you in line. But shame rarely gets anything started. Mostly it makes the next task feel heavier.

slides.title:
You would never
talk to a [[friend]]
this way
slides.body: If a friend forgot their keys, you would not call them useless. You would help them look. You deserve the same tone.

slides.title:
[[Name]] the
voice
slides.body: "That is the old voice again." Naming it reminds you it is a habit, not the truth about you.

slides.title:
Swap [[always]]
for this time
slides.body: Not "I always mess up" but "I missed this one." Smaller words make a smaller problem, and small problems can be solved.

slides.title:
Count what
[[went right]]
slides.body: At night, write down one thing you did today. Just one. Your brain keeps a list of misses. Give it a list of wins too.

slides.title:
Save this for the
next time you are
[[hard on yourself]]
slides.body: You are not a list of mistakes. Dump the noise into my.adhd and get one kind, doable thing back.
